paths.title: Mind & meaning
paths.description: Three approaches to knowledge, perception, and the limits of language.

books.note: Locke develops an account of knowledge grounded in sensation and reflection.
Gibson examines perception through information in the environment and the affordances it offers.
Wittgenstein's numbered propositions explore logic, language, and the limits of what can be said.

paths.title: Japanese literature
paths.description: A small route through Japanese-language fiction in the catalogue.

books.note: In Soseki's Kusamakura, a painter retreats to a mountain hot-spring village in search of detachment.
A Japanese volume pairing Akutagawa's Rashomon and The Nose.
Dazai's No Longer Human, in Japanese.

paths.title: Art & storytelling
paths.description: Explore visual language, narrative structure, and the history of art.

books.note: McCloud explains comics through comics, including closure between panels and the depiction of time.
McKee examines structure and principles of screenwriting.
Gombrich offers a one-volume history of art.
